unit: USD per wire center FCC filing fee
comment: FCC filing fees ONLY (not total compliance cost). Low $375 = Domestic 214 Part 63 Discontinuance, Standard Streamlined Review (payment code CDX); High $1,445 = Part 63 Discontinuance, Non-Standard Review incl. technology-transition filings under 63.71(f)(2)(i) (payment code CDW). Source: FCC 24-137, Order amending 47 CFR 1.1102-1.1109 fee schedule, MD Docket 20-270, released 2025-01-07, https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-24-137A1.pdf (HTTP 200, text matched 2026-10-25). Fees are inflation-adjusted periodically: confirm current amount at 47 CFR 1.1105 https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/section-1.1105 before quoting. No FCC fee for the 47 CFR 51.325/51.329 network change disclosure: FCC 20-116 (MD Docket 20-270) footnote, verbatim: 'We do not propose to adopt a fee for the section 251 network change disclosure filing, which is a notice filing that does not require staff to undertake the same accepted-for-filing process necessary for the 214 applications.' https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-20-116A1_Rcd.pdf (HTTP 200 2026-10-25). Earlier 'para 50' and 'DOC-414725A1' references removed (not verified). Base = NULL: total regulatory compliance cost (legal, notices, state PUC filings) is a PARTNER_DISCOVERY_INPUT per DEC-ROI-FILING-COST.

unit: USD per ROW/street-use permit (base issuance fee; per-ft and hourly add-ons excluded)
comment: Verified official fee schedules (field_cost_benchmark_register, HTTP 200 2026-10-26). Low $209 = Seattle SDOT ROW Simple issuance; High $8,917 = Seattle SDOT Major (SIP/UMP) issuance (https://www.seattle.gov/documents/departments/sdot/street%20use/fee%20information/2025_sdot_street_use_fee_schedule.pdf). Other footprint references: Seattle ROW Complex $754 (utility use codes 51-51E); Minneapolis private utility permit $230 base + $0.07-$1.25/lf (https://www.minneapolismn.gov/business-services/licenses-permits-inspections/streets-sidewalks-utilities/utility-permits/); Portland PBOT main line $7.37/lf, $737 minimum (https://www.portland.gov/transportation/permitting/utility-management). Base NULL: permit mix and count per wire center are a PARTNER_DISCOVERY_INPUT. Denver/Phoenix/Boise: no verified source (GAP-ROW-DEN-PHX-BOI).

unit: fraction of per-line copper O&M avoided after migration to fiber
comment: Low 0.35 = AT&T 2024 Investor Day transcript p.10 (fiber subscriber costs 35% less to maintain than copper). High 0.63 = Analysys Mason 2022 p.35 citing FBA 2020, FTTH opex 50-63% lower per home passed vs HFC/DSL: https://www.analysysmason.com/contentassets/b891ca583e084468baa0b829ced38799/main-report---infra-investment-2022.pdf . Base 0.50 = midpoint (illustrative). Carrier context: AT&T legacy copper direct expense $6B/yr FY2024 est. (Analyst Day slide p.58). Multiply by opex_saved_per_line_year (partner input). Verified text in PDFs by @pm 2026-10-24.

unit: USD copper O&M cost per working copper line per year (BEFORE applying opex_reduction_pct_fiber_vs_copper)
comment: Copper O&M cost per working copper line per year, BEFORE applying opex_reduction_pct_fiber_vs_copper. Annual opex savings = working lines x this value x opex_reduction_pct. LOW 68.53 = cited DERIVED RATIO proxy: FCC SOCC 2006/2007 (ARMIS 43-02/43-08), Qwest Corp (Lumen legacy ILEC in all 6 footprint states). Table 2.8 Acct 6410 Cable & Wire Facilities Expense $826,903K / Table 2.6 switched access lines 12,065,762. BASE 144.45 = same source, Acct 650 Total Plant Specific Operations $1,742,868K / 12,065,762 lines (https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-301505A1.pdf). Caveats: 2006 nominal dollars, not inflated; covers copper AND fiber plant; excludes customer ops/G&A; computed by the agents, not a published FCC per-line figure. HIGH 300 stays SYNTHETIC illustrative (no cited source). is_synthetic stays TRUE because the high bound is synthetic and the low/base values are proxies. Cross-checks (not loaded): Verizon 2006 8-K Ex.99.2 says $110/line NET savings (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/732712/000119312506198669/dex992.htm), already after the fiber reduction; base 144.45 x 0.50 = $72 net. FCC 17-154 n.151 gives $45-$50 per HOME PASSED total savings, a different unit. No footprint PUC publishes a per-line copper O&M figure (field_cost_benchmark_register FP-PUC-COPPER-OM-PER-LINE-GAP), so this remains PARTNER_DISCOVERY_INPUT and is replaced with carrier actuals. Rebased by @data-analyst ACC-DP-OPEX-BENCH-APPLY 2026-10-28 (was synthetic 120/200/300).

comment: No published recovery-rate standard found. Illustrative bounds. Context: Analysys Mason (Nov 2024) reports only a small proportion of deployed copper is recovered and buried plant is often uneconomic: https://www.analysysmason.com/contentassets/918e652a0613478c96bc610266a73b5a/analysys_mason_recovering_copper_emissions_nov2024_rma08_rdfi0.pdf . Confirm with harvesting contractor.

unit: USD/lb
comment: Base = IMF Global price of Copper, 2026-09 monthly avg USD 14,473.06/t (copper_commodity_price_official). Low/high = -20%/+20% sensitivity. Scrap realizations are below benchmark; partner applies buyer discount.

unit: GBP per tonne Cu
comment: Ofcom FOI (2025) citing its 2018 analysis: extraction cost about GBP 2,800/t (= GBP 1.27/lb). UK reference only; not converted to USD (no FX table in scope).

unit: USD per lb Cu recovered (labor + haul + processing)
comment: Illustrative sensitivity bounds bracketing the Ofcom UK anchor (GBP 1.27/lb). Replaces the labor_cost_per_ft GAP: removal cost is quoted per lb recovered until the partner supplies per-sheath-ft contractor rates.

comment: Sale/lease value of vacated CO space; site-specific appraisal.

unit: USD per TCLP lead sample
comment: Value NULL (partner input). Out-of-footprint reference only, not used in calculations: Oklahoma DEQ lab fee schedule FY2026 TCLP extraction + lead = $409/sample (https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/deq/documents/lab/SELSD-SD-008-R3-Lab-Services-Fee-Schedule-FY26.pdf); FY26 ended 2026-06-30 and may be superseded. No footprint-state lab price was found.

unit: USD per ton of lead-sheathed cable (custody, transport, recycle or disposal)
comment: Value NULL (partner input). No verified per-ton price. WA Ecology hazardous waste generation fee ($69/yr) is an annual generator fee, not a per-ton price (https://ecology.wa.gov/waste-toxics/business-waste/reports-fees/hazardous-waste-generation-fee). EPA scrap-metal exclusion (40 CFR 261.4(a)(13), 261.6(a)(3)(ii)) supports recycle-as-scrap pricing (https://www.epa.gov/hw/frequent-questions-related-hazardous-waste-recycling-definition-solid-waste-and-other-exemptions). AZ/MN fees are unverified_detail; CO is a GAP.

comment: Lead-sheath handling adder for v_roi_sensitivity sheath_type=lead (TCLP, custody, disposal). NULL until the partner supplies it; derived outputs stay NULL.

unit: USD per sheath-ft, buried cable removal
comment: REFERENCE_ONLY bracket. low $1.18/LF = FDOT 0633 8 6 multi-conductor communication cable remove (6 contracts, 3,568 LF); high $4.31/LF = FDOT 0633 4 16 telephone cable remove (2 contracts, 5,752 LF; HIGH BOUND ONLY, thin sample, placement not stated). LF-weighted median of the 4 FDOT 0633 removal items = $1.36/LF (0633 1620 underground fiber, 23 contracts, 320,363 LF). FDOT statewide 12-mo 2025-10-01..2026-09-30 p.54-55. CDOT 202-00055 ($3.84/lf) remains unverified_detail and is NOT used. base_value = NULL = PARTNER_DISCOVERY_INPUT (partner supplies contractor $/ft). low/high are REFERENCE_ONLY out-of-footprint brackets from verified_url_200 rows in field_cost_benchmark_register, not copper-OSP contractor pricing; never quote as a base (DEC-REMOVAL-PROXY-REFERENCE-20261031, mirrors DEC-ROI-FILING-COST). Not read by v_roi_sensitivity / payback. Set by @data-analyst 2026-10-31 (ACC-DA-REMOVAL-PROXY-APPLY).

Closest placement match: FDOT 0633 1620 fiber optic cable remove underground $1.36/LF (23 contracts, 320,363 LF). FDOT statewide 12-mo 2025-10-01..2026-09-30 p.54-55. CDOT 202-00040 remains unverified_detail and is NOT used. base_value = NULL = PARTNER_DISCOVERY_INPUT (partner supplies contractor $/ft). low/high are REFERENCE_ONLY out-of-footprint brackets from verified_url_200 rows in field_cost_benchmark_register, not copper-OSP contractor pricing; never quote as a base (DEC-REMOVAL-PROXY-REFERENCE-20261031, mirrors DEC-ROI-FILING-COST). In-between reference: FDOT 0633 1610 fiber optic cable remove overhead $1.33/LF (3 contracts, 4,372 LF, FDOT statewide 12-mo 2025-10-01..2026-09-30 p.54, https://fdotwww.blob.core.windows.net/sitefinity/docs/default-source/fpo/fpc/reports/historicalitemaveragecost/moving/statewide/pdf/historical-item-averages-statewide-12-months.pdf). base_value = NULL = PARTNER_DISCOVERY_INPUT (partner supplies contractor $/ft). low/high are REFERENCE_ONLY out-of-footprint brackets from verified_url_200 rows in field_cost_benchmark_register, not copper-OSP contractor pricing; never quote as a base (DEC-REMOVAL-PROXY-REFERENCE-20261031, mirrors DEC-ROI-FILING-COST). Not read by v_roi_sensitivity / payback. Set by @data-analyst 2026-10-31 (ACC-DA-REMOVAL-PROXY-APPLY).

unit: USD per linear foot of ROW work (variable permit fee, added to the per-permit base)
comment: Verified register rows (verified_url_200). Low $0.07/lf = Minneapolis private utility permit, conduit (MN-MPLS-UTIL-CONDUIT; bored $1.05/lf MN-MPLS-UTIL-BORED, other/open-cut $1.25/lf MN-MPLS-UTIL-OTHER; $230 base per permit) https://www.minneapolismn.gov/business-services/licenses-permits-inspections/streets-sidewalks-utilities/utility-permits/ . High $7.37/lf = Portland PBOT main line with a $737 minimum charge, schedule effective 2026-07-01 (OR-PDX-PBOT-MAINLINE) at source_url. Base NULL: ROW footage and permit mix are a PARTNER_DISCOVERY_INPUT. Per-permit base fees stay in row_permit_usd_each. Minneapolis rates are installation permits; confirm they apply to removal with the city. Seattle has no per-lf fee (it bills $358/hr review). (ACC-DA-ROW-FLAGGER-PARAMS)

unit: USD per flagger-hour (contract bid price), Oregon
comment: ODOT bid item 0223-0168000T FLAGGERS (OR-ODOT-0223-0168000T-AVG-2025, verified_url_200). Index page https://www.oregon.gov/odot/Business/Pages/average_bid_item_prices.aspx. Low $77.19 = 2025 low-bidder weighted average; base $81.34 = 2025 all-bid quantity-weighted average (n=276 bids, 51 contracts); high $82.01 = 2026 YTD average (2026 BID DATA ZIP). These are highway contract prices, so telecom ROW work may differ. Crew cost = flaggers x hours x rate. Use flagger_usd_hour_id for Idaho. (ACC-DA-ROW-FLAGGER-PARAMS)

comment: ITD bid item 626-120A flagger, weighted average (ID-ITD-626-120A-AVG-2025, verified_url_200), computed from the official ITD Average Unit Price XLSX (216,482 bid rows) linked from https://itd.idaho.gov/guide/estimating-qualified-products/.
